questions.q: What is r(0), the ACF at lag 0?
questions.why: A series is perfectly correlated with itself, so r(0) = 1 always.

questions.q: A series has n = 400 points. What is the half-width of the 95% band of the ACF?
The ACF of a series decays very slowly from 0.95 over 30 lags. What is the best next step?
options: Difference the series and plot again
Use the PACF only and ignore the trend
why: Correct: slow decay means trend or random walk. Make the series stationary first.
A very long MA is a poor model for a trending series.
White noise has all bars inside the band.
The trend also distorts the PACF. Fix the series first.

questions.q: ACF cuts off after lag 2. PACF decays smoothly. Which model do you try first?
why: Correct: ACF cut-off after lag q points to MA(q).
AR(2) shows a PACF cut-off, not an ACF cut-off.
An AR(1) has an ACF that decays smoothly, not a cut-off.
White noise has no significant bars at all.

questions.q: In an AR(1) with phi = 0.5, what is the theoretical ACF at lag 3?
questions.why: ACF at lag k is phi^k. 0.5^3 = 0.125.

questions.q: Your hourly electricity data (24 values per day) has ACF spikes at lags 24, 48, 72. What do you do?
options: Add a seasonal difference with lag 24 or a seasonal term with period 24
Remove all data older than 24 hours
why: Correct: the daily pattern repeats every 24 hours, so use season length 24.
Spikes at multiples of 24 are not noise. They are a clear season.
Removing data does not remove the pattern and loses information.
Lag 1 differencing does not remove a repeating daily pattern.

questions.q: You look at 40 lags of the ACF of white noise and see two bars slightly outside the band. What is the right reaction?
options: Expected by chance: about 5% of bars (2 of 40) fall outside a 95% band
The data has a strong season
The data is a random walk
why: Correct: with a 95% band, 1 in 20 bars is outside by chance.
A season gives regular spikes at m, 2m and so on, not random single bars.
A random walk has very slow decay across many lags.
This is normal sampling variation, not a data error.
